definitions.explanation: An interactive educational session where participants actively learn through hands-on activities, discussions, and group work rather than passive listening.
A workplace for artists, craftspeople, or makers to create their works, often also used for teaching.

examples.japanese: プログラミングのワークショップに{参加|さんか}した。
examples.english: I participated in a programming workshop.

examples.japanese: ワークショップで{実際|じっさい}に{手|て}を{動|うご}かして{学|まな}ぶ。
examples.english: At workshops, you learn by actually doing hands-on work.

examples.japanese: アートワークショップで{陶芸|とうげい}を{体験|たいけん}できる。
examples.english: You can experience pottery at the art workshop.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{自宅|じたく}の{一角|いっかく}にワークショップを{設|もう}けている。
examples.english: She has set up a workshop in a corner of her home.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY: From English "workshop." Often abbreviated as WS in Japanese.

USAGE PATTERNS:
・ワークショップを{開催|かいさい}する (to hold a workshop)
・ワークショップに{参加|さんか}する (to participate in a workshop)
・ワークショップ{形式|けいしき} (workshop format)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・ワークショップを{開|ひら}く (to hold a workshop)
・ワークショップの{講師|こうし} (workshop instructor/facilitator)
・{親子|おやこ}ワークショップ (parent-child workshop)
・{体験|たいけん}ワークショップ (hands-on workshop)
・{企業|きぎょう}{研修|けんしゅう}ワークショップ (corporate training workshop)

DIFFERENCE FROM OTHER TERMS:
・{講義|こうぎ} - lecture (one-way, passive)
・{研修|けんしゅう} - training (formal, company-organized)
・セミナー - seminar (may or may not be interactive)
・ワークショップ - workshop (always interactive and participatory)

CONTEXT: Widely used in education, business training, arts, community building, and design thinking. The emphasis on participation and hands-on learning distinguishes it from traditional lectures.
